rejected.title: Writing about play
card: Play is one framework of ideas for creating texts. It covers games, imagination, sport and fun, and asks what play shows about people.
A writer can set a piece in a playground, on a sports field or at a board game table. Play can also be quiet, such as a child inventing a story with toys.
Play often reveals people. How someone plays can show their fears, their loyalties, their need to win or their wish to belong.
A strong piece uses play to say something about people. Describing a game in vivid detail is not enough, and nor is a story about people with no play in it.
rejected.remember: In this framework, the game is the setting and what it reveals about people is the point.

a.q: Which piece best uses play as a framework of ideas?
opts: A story where a cricket game exposes a boy's fear of losing
A story that narrates every over of a cricket final vividly
A poem capturing the sounds and colours of a busy playground
A memoir about a girl's fear of failing her final exams
a.why: The cricket story uses the game to reveal something about a person, so it joins play to an idea about people. The memoir is tempting because it explores fear, but it has no play in it. The other two describe play without saying anything about people.
a.clue: The piece needs both play and an idea about people.

b.q: Tariq plans a piece set at a chess club in Geelong. Which plan most fully explores play as a framework?
opts: Two rivals' moves reveal how each needs to look clever
Two rivals' moves are narrated one by one until checkmate
Every piece on the board is described in close detail
A member's fear of moving house is told without any chess
b.why: The first plan uses the game to show what the players want, so play points to an idea about people. Narrating the rivals' moves is tempting because it has people in it, but it only records the game. The plan without chess is about people but leaves out play.
b.clue: Which plan uses the game to show what the players are like?

draft.title: Writing about play
card: Play is a framework of ideas for creating texts. It covers games, imagination, sport and fun, and asks what people do when they play.
A writer can set a piece in a playground, on a sports field or at a board game table. Play can also be quiet, such as a child inventing a story with toys.
Play often shows people. How someone plays can reveal their fears, their loyalties, their need to win or their wish to belong.
A strong piece uses play to say something about people, not just to describe a game. The game is the setting, and the idea about people is the point.
draft.remember: Play is a framework where the game is the setting and what it shows about people is the point.

a.q: Which piece best uses play as a framework of ideas?
opts: A story where a cricket match shows a boy's fear of failure
A report listing the rules and score of a netball final
A description of the layout of a school playground
A set of instructions for how to play a card game
a.why: The cricket story uses the game to show something about a person. The other options describe or explain play but do not say anything about people, so they stay at the level of the game itself.
a.clue: Look for the piece where the game reveals a person.

b.q: Tariq plans a piece set at a chess club in Geelong. Which plan most fully explores play as a framework?
opts: Two rivals' moves show how each needs to be seen as clever
He describes every piece on the board and how each one moves
He lists the club's history and the names of its members
He explains the steps a beginner takes to win a first game
b.why: The first plan uses chess to reveal what the players want and fear, so the game points to an idea about people. The others stay on facts about the game, even though they are accurate and relate to chess.
b.clue: Ask which plan says something about people, not only about chess.

a.best: A story where a cricket match shows a boy's fear of failure

b.best: Two rivals' moves show how each needs to be seen as clever
